decisions.reason: As a classic door lever handle closely related to the firm's core hardware range, it fits existing design, engineering and sales capabilities, so absorptive capacity is high and there is little reason to withdraw it quickly absent negative signals.
This door lever handle family builds directly on the firm's established knowledge base and broad portfolio logic, making it easy to refine and position across projects rather than remove.

A new door handle design is highly adjacent to the firm's established competencies in ergonomic and design-led fittings, so early market learning can be absorbed and used to improve commercialization.

Because this door handle design is close to the firm's existing offer and supported by its patented engineering and certified systems, management would be inclined to keep it and learn from initial market response.

This handle family extends the firm's system breadth in a familiar category, and a large German producer with in-house R&D would usually retain such a related variant unless performance is clearly poor.

The electronic access system is close to the firm's existing access-control activities and strongly matches its strategic move toward digital building organization, so its related knowledge and R&D base make continuation especially likely.
